questions.q: According to the summary, what does too much confidence lead to?
a: Poor performance and delayed success
Faster learning from early failures
Stronger trust from colleagues
More accurate predictions about the future
questions.why: Lesson 1 states plainly that excessive confidence produces poor performance, citing retail investors and 2008 home buyers.

questions.q: Why does the summary advise against comparing yourself to others?
a: You only see their finished results, not their struggles
Their progress is always faster than yours can be
They are usually hiding how successful they are
Comparison is useful only between close friends
questions.why: Lesson 2 lists three reasons, starting with the fact that you are probably looking at someone's finished product.

questions.q: What does the summary recommend when you make forecasts?
a: Include a broad range of possible outcomes
Commit to the single most likely result
Trust your gut instead of any written plan
Assume the best case will probably happen
questions.why: Lesson 2 says to prepare for both the best and worst outcomes and to forecast across a wide range of probabilities.

questions.q: How does the summary describe people who try to fake confidence?
a: They feel a need to show off and be noticed
They avoid attention and praise whenever possible
They are quick to admit what they do not know
They rarely care what other people think of them
questions.why: The overview says people faking confidence need to show off or be seen, while truly confident people do not.

questions.q: What is the relationship between skill and confidence, according to the summary?
a: Skill builds confidence, not the other way around
Confidence comes first and then creates skill
The two grow separately and rarely affect each other
Confidence can replace skill once it is convincing enough
questions.why: Lesson 3 says skill builds self-worth and that confidence has to be backed up by real ability.
